headline: Suffield school bus crash sends 11 to hospitals with minor injuries
dek: A Region 12 bus carrying students left South Grand Street and struck a building Thursday morning; police said the cause remains under investigation.
body: Eleven people were taken to two local hospitals with minor injuries Thursday after a small school bus carrying students left the roadway and struck a building in Suffield, Connecticut. The crash brought police, fire and ambulance crews to South Grand Street and left investigators working to determine why the bus veered off the road.

Suffield police said officers responded to the area of 425 South Grand St. at about 9:49 a.m. after receiving a report of a motor-vehicle crash with possible injuries. Their preliminary account said the bus was traveling north toward Mountain Road when it left the right shoulder and collided with a building beside the street. Police did not announce a mechanical problem, medical event, weather factor or other cause.

The bus came from Regional School District 12, which serves communities in the Shepaug Valley. NBC Connecticut reported that students were aboard, while the Suffield Volunteer Ambulance Association said 15 people, including the driver, were on the small bus. The association said 10 students and the driver were transported for evaluation. Authorities did not release the students’ ages or identify the hospitals.

The ambulance response required help from several nearby agencies. The ambulance association said it sent three ambulances staffed by paramedics, while Enfield EMS and the Windsor Locks Lions Club Ambulance provided additional units. North Central CMED helped coordinate the transports and contacted receiving hospitals to confirm that they could accommodate the patients.

That coordination also shaped how the students were handled after the crash. According to the ambulance association’s statement reported by Patch, responders tried to keep the students together when possible so school staff and families could receive information more easily. Region 12 personnel came to the scene to assist the students, and emergency officials said the response was managed through the area’s normal mutual-aid system.

The ambulance association also pushed back on online descriptions of the incident as a mass-casualty or multi-casualty event. It said the scene required significant coordination but did not meet that designation. That distinction describes the emergency-management classification, not the seriousness of the reported injuries: police and ambulance officials said everyone taken for treatment had minor injuries.

Hearst Connecticut Media reported that the bus was carrying Shepaug Valley School students on the way to a fair and that a Region 12 official said the vehicle was driven by a properly licensed teacher. That account adds context to the trip but does not resolve the central unanswered question of what caused the bus to leave South Grand Street. Police interviewed people involved and said the investigation was continuing.

South Grand Street was closed while the scene was investigated and later reopened, according to local reports. No charges or citations had been announced in the available accounts. For families and residents, the immediate outcome was that the 11 people transported for care had reported minor injuries; the longer-term questions concern the crash sequence, the condition of the building and any findings by police or the school district. Sources: [Suffield Police Department details reported by Patch](https://patch.com/connecticut/suffield/crash-reported-south-grand-street-suffield), [NBC Connecticut](https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/11-people-sent-to-hospitals-after-school-bus-crashes-into-building-in-suffield/3780574/), [WFSB](https://www.wfsb.com/2026/10/01/school-bus-crashes-into-building-suffield-police-confirm/), and [Hearst Connecticut Media](https://www.stamfordadvocate.com/journalinquirer/article/region-12-school-bus-crash-suffield-ct-south-grand-22457938.php).
